newsitem.title: CANADA: Aber says Diavik diamond values rise.
newsitem.headline: Aber says Diavik diamond values rise.

text.p: Aber Resources Ltd said Wednesday diamonds from its Diavik property in Canada's Northwest Territories were given a sharply higher value by independent Belgian experts than previously estimated.
The company said a 5,658 carat representative sample of diamonds from the A154 South kimberlite pipe at Diavik was valued at an average of US$67 a carat.

The valuation, done by six independent diamantaires in Antwerp, Belgium, was higher than US$59.30 a carat previously estimated by CRA Diamonds Ltd of Australian based on a valuation of 8,979 carats from the same bulk sample.
"In commenting on the diamonds, the diamantaires were unanimous in their view that the diamonds are attractive, of high quality and readily marketable," Aber said.
Aber has 40 percent of the project and Anglo-British mining concern RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd the rest.

Analysts have said that ever-more promising results from the property suggest it is almost certain to yield a diamond mine. Diavik neighbors the Lac de Gras site where Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and Canada's Dia Met Minerals Ltd are already building a diamond mine.
Aber has the right to market its share of the production independently of its partners.

Aber said that preliminary modelling for the A154 South kimberlite property at Diavik increased the resource from 11 million to 12 million tonnes to 400 metres below the lake level. The grade was about 4.2 carats a tonne compared to an earlier reported drill hole grade of 4.5 carats a tonne.
Geological resource models are being generated for each of pipes A-154 South, A-154 North, A-418 and A-21. Revised tonnage and grade estimates will be available in mid-summer 1997, Aber said.
A C$80 million pre-feasibility study at Diavik is slated to be completed in the autumn.
